long_biography.plain_text:
A meeting with Japanese garment entrepreneur Noriyuki Matsuoka changed the scale of Li Qinfu's small Zhejiang workshop. Li had entered factory work in his early twenties and taken charge of the indebted garment operation in 1983. Matsuoka's investment brought capital and export access, while the joint venture adopted his name. The business grew from uniform manufacturing into specialist printing, paper and related industrial activities.

The listed company's next phase moved beyond manufacturing. Li developed Nine Dragons Hill on Hangzhou Bay as a mixed property, tourism and leisure project, placing real estate at the centre of his business interests. His related companies extended into investment, resort property and tourism development across Shanghai, Hong Kong and Zhejiang. His public-company board role ended in 2015; privately controlled property and tourism companies still held interests in the Nine Dragons project at that point.

The immutable first_name and last_name fields are reversed relative to that structure, so corrections are proposed without changing the display order. Qin Fu and Qinfu search variants were reviewed but not merged unless the Matsuoka and Nine Dragons identity chain also matched.

Li Qinfu is not unique in romanized search results. The resolved person is anchored by Chinese nationality, Shanghai residence, age approximately 58 in 2020, Chinese characters 李勤夫, Pinghu/Matsuoka history and the documented transition into Nine Dragons companies. Academic authors, UK company officers and people transliterated from different Chinese characters were excluded.

review.notes: Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Commercial printing: Specialist printing became a material industrial activity within Matsuoka under Li's leadership rather than a minor investment holding. [2] Cross-border joint ventures: A joint venture with Japanese garment entrepreneur Noriyuki Matsuoka supplied the capital, name and export access that changed Li's business scale. [3] Export-led manufacturing expansion: Matsuoka's scale was built through Japanese-market uniform exports and broader export-manufacturing growth. [4] Founder-led public company: Li led the listed Matsuoka and successor Nine Dragons platform through its manufacturing and later property-and-tourism phases. [5] Hospitality executive: Li held chair roles across resort-property, tourism and leisure companies associated with Nine Dragons Hill. [6] Leisure real estate: Leisure property was a material component of the Nine Dragons Hill development and Li's later private-company interests. [7] Manufacturing entrepreneur: Li was the founder-operator who transformed an indebted workshop into the diversified Matsuoka manufacturing group. [8] Manufacturing executive: Li led Matsuoka as chairman and chief executive during its expansion from garments into printing and adjacent industrial activities. [9] Manufacturing-to-real-estate transition: Li redirected the listed platform from export manufacturing and printing toward property, tourism and leisure development. [10] Matsuoka Group: Matsuoka Group was the export-oriented garment, textile and printing business that Li founded and scaled into his original industrial fortune. [11] Multi-sector owner-operator: Li repeatedly combined ownership and operating control across manufacturing, printing, property, investment, tourism and leisure businesses. [12] Nine Dragons Hill: Nine Dragons Hill was the defining mixed property, tourism and leisure development around which Li reorganised his later business platform. [13] Real estate executive: Li chaired and controlled companies responsible for the Nine Dragons property-development platform. [14] Real-estate owner-operator: Li combined controlling ownership with active chairmanship and development responsibility across the Nine Dragons property companies. [15] Shanghai Nine Dragons Tourism: Shanghai Nine Dragons Tourism was the listed company through which Li led the later property, tourism and leisure phase of his business career. [16] Textile manufacturing: Textile production was a defining component of the Matsuoka industrial group that created Li's original wealth. [17] Township-enterprise entrepreneur: Li's defining entrepreneurial start came from taking responsibility for and transforming a small indebted Zhejiang township garment workshop. [18] Travel entrepreneur: Li expanded from industry into entrepreneurship centred on a destination tourism and leisure platform. [19] Uniform manufacturing: Uniform production for export markets was the specific garment-manufacturing route through which Li first expanded Matsuoka.
